alt: A 2019 Ford F-250 Super Duty XLT pickup truck in white, parked on a paved surface, showing its large front grille, raised ride height, and dual rear wheels
story: Ford issued recall 26C46 on October 6, 2026, covering 102,159 F-Series trucks (2025–2026 F-150 through F-750) because the analog speedometer and tachometer can stick or swing to wrong readings; Ford's own filing admits the trucks meet FMVSS 101 (which governs speedometer placement and labeling) but may not meet the standard's 'full intent' — because the federal regulation does not require passenger-car speedometers to be accurate.
why_funny: America's best-selling truck, priced up to $90,000+, shipped with a speedometer that can lie to you, and the only reason it's being recalled is that Ford felt bad about the spirit of the law it technically didn't break.
